note: Public offset alerts shown on the website. This file is the permanent record: never delete an item. The site shows only items whose 'added' date is within the last three weeks of 'updated' (at least eight items are always shown), so older items fall away from the pages but stay here. 'date' is when the event happened (YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM if only the month is known); 'added' is the date the item went on the site; 'tag' is optional ('Civil' or 'Rules'). Summaries are Capital's own words; every item must link to its original source. Internal scores, suggested services and verdicts from the Offset Opportunity Monitor never go here.

items.title: Peru moves to fund a second batch of 12 F-16 Block 70 fighters
items.summary: Peru's government has asked Congress for extra credit to pay for a second batch of 12 F-16s from Lockheed Martin, taking the fleet to 24. The money must be spent this fiscal year, so a contract is expected before the end of 2026. Peru's industrial compensation rules apply to foreign defence purchases of this size, and Lockheed Martin set out a proposed offset package in August.

items.title: Romania orders 12 Airbus H225M helicopters under the EU's SAFE defence loans
items.summary: Airbus has announced an order from Romania for 12 H225M helicopters, placed through the French armaments agency and funded by the EU's SAFE loans, with the Romanian maker IAR as its long-term partner. Romania's technological and industrial cooperation rules cover government-to-government purchases, and the Brașov workforce has already questioned how much work will come to Romania.

items.title: Colombian Army opens a US$34.5m tender for light transport aircraft
items.summary: The Colombian Army has published a tender, with offers due on 26 October, to replace three retired C-212 transports. The Czech L-410 NG is reported as the front-runner. Colombia's 2025 decree on industrial offsets applies to defence contracts from about US$3 million.

items.title: Austria weighs seven fighter types to replace its early Eurofighters
items.summary: The Austrian armed forces are assessing seven candidate aircraft, including Boeing's F-15EX, as a successor to the Tranche 1 Eurofighters. Austria now agrees industrial cooperation case by case on its major purchases, so a fighter buy would be its largest such negotiation yet.

items.title: Malaysia's Budget 2027 funds a RM3.4bn rail overhaul and 42 new trains
items.summary: Budget 2027 gives Prasarana more than RM3.4 billion to rehabilitate its urban rail network and funds 42 new train sets for the ETS and KTM Komuter services. Malaysia's Industrial Collaboration Programme applies to purchases paid with federal funds worth RM50 million or more from foreign contractors, which usually includes rolling stock and signalling.

items.title: India's Air Force seeks proposals for 60 medium transport aircraft
items.summary: The Indian Air Force has issued a request for proposals for 60 medium transport aircraft, with responses due by December. Embraer with Mahindra and Lockheed Martin with Tata are the expected bidders, and both plan Indian assembly. India's draft 2026 procurement rules would replace offsets with a 30% Indian-content requirement on global purchases.

items.title: Denmark takes delivery of the first of four new air defence systems
items.summary: Denmark's defence procurement agency has received the first of four ground-based air defence systems bought under a DKK 58.2 billion programme, with support contracts still to be signed. Denmark assesses industrial co-operation case by case on purchases from foreign suppliers worth more than DKK 50 million.

items.title: Greece signs for two Italian FREMM frigates with Greek shipyard work included
items.summary: Greece and Italy have signed the arrangement transferring the frigates Carlo Bergamini and Virginio Fasan to the Hellenic Navy in 2028 and 2029. The agreement provides for Greek industry to take part in maintenance and in integrating new systems, in line with Greece's push for 25% domestic participation in new armament programmes.

items.title: Malaysia's offset cap on CPTPP-covered purchases falls from 60% to 40% on 28 November
items.summary: Under Malaysia's schedule to the CPTPP trade pact, which took effect for Malaysia on 29 November 2022, offset credits on purchases by the covered ministries are capped at 60% of contract value for the first four years, then 40% until the end of the eighth year, 20% until the twelfth, and none after that. The first step down therefore falls on 28 November 2026. Defence purchases are largely outside the pact, so the full Industrial Collaboration Programme still applies to them.

items.title: Still no government response on the UK's planned defence offsets regime
items.summary: The Ministry of Defence's written consultation on a defence offsets regime closed on 23 December 2025. As of 13 October 2026 the consultation page still says the feedback is being analysed, and no outcome has been published. Overseas suppliers bidding into UK programmes should plan for UK workshare and industrial participation commitments while the rules are settled.

items.title: Canada takes next step with Saab on GlobalEye early-warning aircraft
items.summary: Canada is moving ahead with Saab, its preferred supplier, towards a contract for six GlobalEye airborne early warning and control aircraft. Defence purchases of this size normally carry obligations under Canada's Industrial and Technological Benefits (ITB) policy.

items.title: US approves possible sale of 21 Black Hawk helicopters to Norway
items.summary: The US has notified a possible sale of 21 UH-60M Black Hawk helicopters to Norway, valued at about US$2.3 billion. Norway's industrial cooperation rules normally apply to foreign defence purchases of this size.

items.title: Boeing signs Apache offset agreements with Polish industry
items.summary: Boeing has signed offset agreements with the Polish companies WZL-1 and WCBKT covering training and sustainment for Poland's AH-64E Apache fleet.

items.title: US approves possible APKWS II laser-guided rocket sale to Saudi Arabia
items.summary: A possible sale of APKWS II laser guidance kits to Saudi Arabia, valued at about US$1.96 billion, has been notified. Saudi Arabia's industrial participation programme, run by GAMI, aims to localise a growing share of defence spending.

items.title: US approves possible sale of 155mm artillery shells to Norway
items.summary: A possible sale of 155mm M795 high-explosive shells to Norway, valued at about US$270 million, has been notified.

items.title: TKMS chosen as preferred bidder for Canada's new submarines
items.summary: Canada has selected Germany's TKMS as preferred bidder for up to 12 Type 212CD submarines under the Canadian Patrol Submarine Project. Contract negotiations, including industrial benefits for Canada, now follow.

items.title: Swiss F-35A offset programme expected to exceed its targets
items.summary: The Swiss government reports further offset projects placed with Swiss industry under the F-35A purchase, and expects the agreed offset targets to be clearly exceeded.

items.title: Canada and Australia partner on Arctic over-the-horizon radar
items.summary: Canada has agreed a partnership with Australia to deliver the Arctic Over-the-Horizon Radar, part of Canada's plan to modernise NORAD.

items.title: Swiss Armaments Programme 2026 includes more IRIS-T SLM air defence
items.summary: The Federal Council's Armaments Programme 2026 asks Parliament to fund additional IRIS-T SLM ground-based air defence systems. Swiss offset rules apply to defence purchases from foreign suppliers.
